question: Thinking of buying a block in Perth. How do I find out if it's on some kind of contaminated land list, and do I have to pay to check?
note: Casual (landowner). DWER 2025 section 9.1, Table 24 (printed 57): the online contaminated sites database is free; a basic summary of records costs $44 by Form 2. Printed 59 (section 9.1.2) says what the database covers and to check the register if a site is not listed; printed 58 covers the Landgate report.

question: we're selling our house and it's been classified contaminated, restricted use. do we legally have to tell the buyer or is that optional?
note: Casual (landowner). DWER 2025 section 10.1 (printed 62): the owner must give written disclosure on Form 6 at least 14 days before completion for this classification. Printed 63 continues (Form 6 signed, a copy to the department).

question: Got a letter saying my land is 'possibly contaminated'. Can I fight that decision, and how long do I get?
note: Casual (landowner). DWER 2025 section 7.6, Table 14 (printed 39): the owner can appeal; the Act gives at least 21 days and the notice often allows 45.

question: Sorry if this is a silly question, but if a soil sample comes back over the guideline number, does that automatically mean the whole site has to be cleaned up?
note: Casual (non-expert visitor). ASC NEPM B1 section 2.1.2 (printed 4): investigation and screening levels are not clean-up levels; they trigger a site-specific look. Section 3.2.2 (printed 20) says what an exceedance leads to. DWER 2021 section 10.4 (printed 44) gives the same Tier 1 logic.

question: our farm is right next to an old gold mine. could the dirt just naturally have loads of arsenic and lead in it without anyone polluting it?
note: Casual (landowner). ASC NEPM B1 section 1.5, Mineralised areas (printed 2). DWER 2021 printed 62 (mine sites and mineralised areas: background naturally high, with a warning about disturbed mine waste) and printed 11 (disturbance of naturally occurring substances).

question: first ever PFAS groundwater sampling job tomorrow! am I ok to wear sunscreen and my brand new waterproof jacket, or will that stuff up the samples?
note: Casual (new graduate). PFAS NEMP 3.0 section 18.2.2, Preventing sample contamination (printed 165): new clothing, treated fabrics, water-resistant products and sunscreen are on the cross-contamination list; printed 166 says they should not be worn or used during sampling.

question: Is it only drinking the water that matters with PFAS, or is having a shower in it a problem too?
note: Casual (non-expert visitor). ADWG PFAS fact sheet, General description: oral ingestion is the main route; inhalation and skin exposure while showering and bathing are considered negligible. Web page, no page numbers.

question: Does ordinary tap water in Australia actually have PFAS in it?

sections: Levels detected in Australian drinking water

note: Casual (landowner). ADWG PFAS fact sheet, Levels detected in Australian drinking water: most distributed supplies have low or negligible PFAS; the per-chemical subsections give ranges. Subsections count.

question: can a water filter or reverse osmosis actually get PFAS out of water, or does normal treatment already do it?
note: Casual (landowner). ADWG PFAS fact sheet, Treatment of drinking water: standard treatment is mostly ineffective; GAC, ion exchange and high-pressure membranes are used, and reverse osmosis removes over 99% of long-chain PFAS. PFAS NEMP 3.0 Appendix D, Table D1 (printed 229 and 230) lists adsorption and reverse osmosis as available.

question: They've started drilling holes at the old petrol station next door to us. Is anyone meant to tell the neighbours what's going on?
note: Casual (neighbour). DWER 2021 section 14.4 (printed 94): at the detailed site investigation stage, tell stakeholders what to expect (drilling, hours, noise, who is doing the work, contacts); section 14.2 (printed 92) names nearby residents as stakeholders. DWER 2025 section 9.3 (printed 61) covers the same point.

question: what's the deal with auditors for contaminated land in WA? like when do you actually have to get one involved?
note: Casual (new graduate). DWER 2021 section 4.2 (printed 6): accredited contaminated sites auditors and when a mandatory auditor's report is required; printed 7 quotes regulation 31 and s.44 in full.

question: They're cleaning up an old fuel depot near us. Can the dirt they dig out be trucked off and used as fill somewhere else?
note: Casual (landowner). DWER 2021 section 12.9, Re-use of excavated soil (printed 82): excavated soil may be reused on or off site if characterised as suitable; also the clean fill and uncontaminated fill definitions.

question: After an owner confirms their site is contaminated, how many days do they have to notify DWER, and does suspected contamination run on the same clock?
note: Practitioner, table page. DWER 2025 section 6.4, Table 8 (printed 27): known contamination within 21 days; suspected contamination as soon as reasonably practicable.

question: DWER has rated our site high priority. By when are the PSI, the DSI and any remedial action plan expected?
note: Practitioner, table page. DWER 2025 section 8.3.1, Table 20 (printed 52): PSI within three months, DSI within six, RAP within nine. Printed 51 introduces the table.

question: What has to go in with a Form 3 request for a certificate of contamination audit, and what is the fee?
note: Practitioner. DWER 2025 section 12.2 (printed 68): title, technical and remediation reports, a mandatory auditor's report, a classification recommendation and the prescribed fee ($6,050 as at 30 June 2024).

question: Is purging and sampling monitoring wells with a bailer acceptable on a WA contaminated site job, or does DWER expect something else?
note: Practitioner. DWER 2021 section 9.6, Groundwater sampling methods (printed 36): bailers and high speed pumps are not recommended because they agitate the groundwater and alter the sample.

question: A lot has brick and concrete rubble in the fill plus some discolouration and odour, but nothing above screening levels. Does that on its own make it reportable to DWER?
note: Practitioner. DWER 2021 section 7.2, Aesthetics (printed 23 and 24): a site affected only by aesthetic issues need not be reported as known or suspected contaminated. The DWER 2025 Table 1 footnote (printed 8) says the same.

question: For a house lot with a veggie garden, what soil value applies to PFOS plus PFHxS, and how does it change if the household grows around half of its fruit and veg?
note: Practitioner, table page. PFAS NEMP 3.0 section 8.6, Table 5 (printed 50): HIL A 0.003 mg/kg for the sum of PFOS and PFHxS; at 50% home-grown produce the example screening value is 0.001 mg/kg.

question: We want to send PFAS-impacted soil to an unlined landfill. What leachable and total concentrations does it have to be under?
note: Practitioner, table page. PFAS NEMP 3.0 section 14.6, Table 11 (printed 141): unlined, ASLP 0.07 ug/L for PFOS plus PFHxS and 0.56 ug/L for PFOA; totals 20 mg/kg and 50 mg/kg; the waste must be under both.

question: Is there a guideline value for PFOS in fish that birds or mammals eat, as opposed to fish people eat?
note: Practitioner, table page. PFAS NEMP 3.0 section 8.7, Table 7 Biota guideline values (printed 57): wildlife diet values for mammals and birds, plus a whole bird egg value.

question: On a PFAS program, how often should blind duplicates and rinsate blanks go in relative to primary samples? Is the usual 1 in 20 enough?
note: Practitioner. PFAS NEMP 3.0 section 18.2 (printed 161 and 162): QC more often than the NEPM one in 20, with replicates, splits, spikes and rinsates at least one per 10 primary samples. Appendix B, Table B3 (printed 216) gives frequencies per QC sample type.

question: What waste code and dangerous goods class go on the paperwork when trucking PFAS-contaminated spoil?
note: Practitioner. PFAS NEMP 3.0 section 11.1 (printed 103): waste code M270, organic chemical category; PFAS-contaminated material is Dangerous Goods Class 9.

question: What percentage weight for weight of bonded asbestos in soil triggers further assessment on a standard residential block with a garden?
note: Practitioner, table page. ASC NEPM B1 section 4.8, Table 7 (printed 30): bonded ACM 0.01% w/w for Residential A.

question: When deriving ecological levels for metals, how long does contamination need to have been in the soil before the aged values can be used?
note: Practitioner. ASC NEPM B1 section 2.5.9 (printed 15): at least two years counts as aged; the footnotes to the EIL tables (printed 60 to 63) repeat it. DWER 2021 printed 58 says the same.
